## Intersection
The `.intersection()` method returns a **new set** containing elements that exist in **both sets**.

```ts
const a = new Set(["alice", "bob", "carol"]);
const b = new Set(["bob", "dave", "alice"]);
const c = a.intersection(b);
console.log(c); // Set { 'alice', 'bob' }
```

## Difference
The `.difference()` method returns a **new set** containing elements that are in the **first set but not in the second**.

```ts
const d = a.difference(b);
console.log(d); // Set { 'carol' }
```

## Union
The `.union()` method returns a **new set** containing all elements from both sets (duplicates removed).

```ts
const e = a.union(b);
console.log(e); // Set { 'alice', 'bob', 'carol', 'dave' }
```

## Assignment (MCQ)

2. Find elements in the first set but not the second
3. Find all elements from both sets
